title: quantile-aware burst capacity balancer and utilization probe
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Dedicated customers see unpredictable microburst tail behavior where a small subset of tenants at the 95-99th percentile generate short-lived demand spikes that either starve other tenants or cause overly conservative headroom and wasted capacity. This PR introduces a Quantile-Aware Burst Capacity Balancer (QAB) plus a lightweight utilization probe to (1) allocate transient burst credits based on observed percentile demand, (2) smooth credit assignment to avoid oscillation, and (3) surface percentile telemetry for SLO tuning.

Design summary: QAB runs as a controller in the dedicated control plane. It continuously consumes aggregated per-tenant token and concurrency time-series and computes target burst budgets per tenant using configurable quantiles (default: p95 for transient eligibility, p99 for saturation guard). Credits are applied as short-lived soft reservations on the scheduler (no hard preemption) with an EWMA-based decay and a bounded top-up algorithm to prevent starvation. The utilization probe collects streaming quantile estimates with a T-Digest and publishes metrics that include tenant_p95_rps, tenant_p99_rps, burst_credit_balance, and tenant_tail_latency_ms. A new feature flag (experimental.quantile_balancer=true) gates the runtime behavior until rollout.

Key behaviors and guarantees: - Priority fairness preserved: soft reservations are normalized by tenant weight and will not exceed an adjustable percent of cluster spare capacity. - Contention resolution: when spare capacity is insufficient, the balancer reduces allocations to lower-priority tenants based on rank and historical utilization delta. - Safety hooks: a global circuit-breaker reverts to static burst policy when probe latency or data gaps occur.

Changes included: - Controller implementation: pkg/autoscaler/qab_controller.go, pkg/autoscaler/burst_allocator.go - Telemetry: internal/telemetry/quantiles.go, pkg/metrics/registrar.go (new metrics and labels) - Scheduler integration: pkg/scheduler/soft_reservation.go (apply/remove soft reservations, no new hard preemption code) - CLI and config: cmd/cli/capacity_balancer.go, examples/dedicated/balancer-config.yaml - Charts and ops: charts/dedicated/values.yaml updated to include defaults + feature flag, docs/operational/runbooks/dedicated/burst-balancer.md - Tests: tests/e2e/burst_balancer_test.go (synthetic spike scenarios), unit tests for allocator logic and probe.

Rollback and rollout plan: deploy behind feature flag in canary region with 10% of dedicated fleet enabled; monitor tenant_p99_rps and cluster_saturation_pct. Rollback criteria: increase in 99th percentile latency by >15% for any tenant for 5 consecutive minutes or spike in eviction_count > 3x baseline. Rollout stages documented in the runbook; automatic fallback to static policy if the telemetry probe reports >1% sample loss.

Performance and validation: e2e synthetic tests show reduced headroom requirement by ~8% on steady-state workloads while reducing 95th->99th latency amplification during bursts by ~18% for medium-weight tenants. CPU and memory overhead of the controller is negligible at cluster scale (measured ~25MB heap, 3% CPU at 1k tenants).

Operational notes: expose tenant_p95_rps and tenant_p99_rps in Console per-tenant dashboard; add alerting rules for tenant_tail_latency_ms and burst_credit_balance depletion. The runbook contains recommended quantile and smoothing defaults for different customer SLAs.

Security and compatibility: no changes to authentication or RBAC. The controller requires read access to aggregated telemetry and write access to the scheduler soft-reservation API; a new minimal role is described in docs/operational/runbooks/dedicated/burst-balancer.md.

Follow-ups: - ENG-3501: automated tuning job to suggest quantile thresholds per-customer - ENG-3583: policy UI in Console to preview quantile allocations - Add an integration test covering multi-cluster spillover in a future PR.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation and unit tests - [x] E2E synthetic scenarios - [x] Documentation and runbook - [x] Chart values and feature flag - [x] Rollout + rollback plan

Related: referenced SUP-1298 (support case where tenant experienced repeated microburst-induced throttles); ties to ENG-3472 (autoscaler extensibility work).

review_comments: Martin Green: Can we avoid holding a global lock during allocation cycles? Please try a sharded lock or read-copy-update to reduce contention.
Aisha Patel: Switched to sharded mutex map (allocator_shards) as suggested, added benchmark in allocator_test.go showing sub-ms latency per allocation cycle.
Sofia Kim: We should ensure the feature flag can be toggled at runtime without restart; please confirm chart values and controller watch for flag changes.
Aisha Patel: Feature flag backed by a ConfigMap watch; documented behavior in charts and runbook. Added a small e2e to toggle flag mid-run.
Diego Alvarez: Minor: add more descriptive metric labels for tenant id and weight; otherwise LGTM.
Martin Green: Verified tests and e2e in canary, approving once CI passes.
release_notes: Introduces Quantile-Aware Burst Capacity Balancer: dynamic short-lived soft reservations based on tenant p95/p99 demand, new percentile telemetry (tenant_p95_rps, tenant_p99_rps, tenant_tail_latency_ms), and a controlled rollout behind a feature flag. Improves tail-behavior during microbursts and reduces steady-state headroom in many workloads.
